description: A conservative cross-industry pack extracted from recurring concepts in the retail and financial-services libraries. Every item is a research hypothesis, not proof of intent.

signals.label: Recent funding or growth-capital event
signals.query_template: "{{company_name}}" (raised OR funding OR investment OR recapitalization) site:{{company_domain}} OR site:businesswire.com OR site:prnewswire.com
signals.applicability: Private or sponsor-backed companies where a dated capital event is publicly confirmed.
disqualifiers: No relevance to the campaign objective
signals.safe_interpretation: The company has publicly announced new capital and stated uses of funds may guide research priorities.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim budget availability, purchase intent, or urgency unless the source states it.
signals.rationale: Capital events can change priorities, but only the stated use of funds is evidence.

signals.label: New executive in a function relevant to the campaign
signals.query_template: "{{company_name}}" (appoints OR names OR hires OR joins) (chief OR president OR vice-president OR VP OR head OR director) site:{{company_domain}}
signals.applicability: Any company when the role directly owns the operating area addressed by the campaign.
disqualifiers: Role has no connection to the campaign
Only a scraped profile is available
signals.safe_interpretation: A relevant leadership change can justify researching whether priorities or operating plans changed.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not say a new leader will replace vendors, has budget, or is dissatisfied.
signals.rationale: Leadership transitions create a research window, not automatic buying intent.

signals.label: Cluster of open roles connected to the campaign problem
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (careers OR jobs) ("{{company_name}}") (engineer OR manager OR director OR lead)
signals.applicability: Any company with multiple current first-party job postings tied to the campaign's operating area.
disqualifiers: Third-party repost without an active company listing
signals.safe_interpretation: Active hiring shows the company is investing attention or capacity in the named function.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim the team is understaffed, funded for a vendor, or unable to build internally.
signals.rationale: A role cluster is stronger than a single posting and remains portable across sectors.

signals.label: Material product or capability launch
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (launches OR introduces OR announces OR unveils) (product OR platform OR capability OR feature)
signals.applicability: Any company with a dated first-party launch relevant to the campaign objective.
disqualifiers: No connection to the campaign problem
signals.safe_interpretation: The launch creates a concrete change in product surface, audience, or operating requirements worth researching.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim adoption, success, internal difficulty, or unmet demand without evidence.
signals.rationale: Launches are observable changes; relevance depends on the campaign.

signals.label: New integration, API, or platform ecosystem
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (integration OR API OR developer OR marketplace OR partner) (launches OR announces OR available)
signals.applicability: Companies exposing new integration surfaces, developer tools, marketplaces, or partner programs.
disqualifiers: Directory listing with no dated change
signals.safe_interpretation: The company is expanding how external systems or partners connect to its product.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim integration gaps, partner dissatisfaction, or implementation complexity.
signals.rationale: Ecosystem changes are common across software and service businesses.

signals.label: New geographic market or operating region
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (expands OR expansion OR launches OR opens) (market OR region OR country OR office)
signals.applicability: Companies announcing entry into a new country, region, or materially different market.
signals.safe_interpretation: Expansion can introduce localization, demand, operational, or partner questions that merit research.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim the expansion is struggling or that a specific capability is required.
signals.rationale: Geographic growth is portable, but the consequence must be campaign-specific.

signals.label: Pricing or packaging change
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (pricing OR plans OR packaging OR edition OR tier) (new OR update OR change OR usage)
signals.applicability: Companies with a dated, observable change to plans, packaging, usage limits, or commercial model.
disqualifiers: Current pricing page with no evidence of change
signals.safe_interpretation: A commercial-model change may alter acquisition, conversion, expansion, or enablement requirements.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim churn, customer confusion, or revenue pressure without evidence.
signals.rationale: Pricing and packaging changes affect GTM systems across industries.

signals.label: Expansion into a new customer segment
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (enterprise OR mid-market OR small-business OR SMB OR vertical OR industry) (launches OR expands OR solution OR offering)
signals.applicability: Companies explicitly targeting a new company-size, buyer, or vertical segment.
disqualifiers: No dated evidence of a new motion
signals.safe_interpretation: A new segment changes the audience, proof, channel, or operating requirements worth validating.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim the existing motion is failing or that the new segment has converted.
signals.rationale: Segment change is a direct GTM research signal independent of industry.

signals.label: Leadership names a strategic operating priority
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (strategy OR priorities OR roadmap OR transformation) (CEO OR president OR founder OR annual OR investor)
signals.applicability: Any company where an authorized leader names a priority in a dated first-party source.
signals.safe_interpretation: The named priority is safe context for a research question tied to the campaign.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not equate a stated priority with budget, timeline, vendor evaluation, or operational pain.
signals.rationale: First-party priorities are stronger than generic intent proxies.

signals.label: Public technology, channel, or services partnership
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (partnership OR partners OR alliance OR collaboration) (announces OR selected OR expands)
signals.applicability: Companies announcing a material partner relationship relevant to the campaign.
signals.safe_interpretation: The announcement shows an externally stated area of collaboration.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not infer contract value, implementation status, satisfaction, exclusivity, or replacement intent.
signals.rationale: Partnerships reveal declared direction but require careful scope boundaries.

signals.label: Acquisition, merger, or divestiture
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (acquires OR acquisition OR merger OR combines OR divestiture)
signals.applicability: Companies with a confirmed corporate transaction relevant to the campaign workflow.
signals.safe_interpretation: A transaction can create integration, positioning, customer, or operating questions worth researching.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not assert integration problems, layoffs, tool consolidation, or budget without evidence.
signals.rationale: Corporate change is portable; the operating consequence must be sourced or framed as a question.

signals.label: Repeated, recent customer-friction pattern
signals.query_template: "{{company_name}}" (review OR support OR complaint OR issue) (site:reddit.com OR site:trustpilot.com OR site:g2.com OR site:capterra.com)
signals.applicability: Companies with multiple recent, independent examples of the same relevant customer problem.
signals.safe_interpretation: A repeated public pattern can justify a bounded hypothesis and a request to validate it.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not present reviews as internal metrics, a company-wide failure, or proof of purchase intent.
signals.rationale: Friction is useful only when repeated, recent, relevant, and carefully qualified.

signals.label: Security, privacy, or compliance milestone
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (SOC 2 OR ISO 27001 OR GDPR OR HIPAA OR PCI OR compliance OR security) (certified OR launches OR announces OR report)
signals.applicability: Companies publishing a dated certification, trust-center change, governance program, or compliance expansion.
signals.safe_interpretation: The company has made a visible trust or governance investment that may affect evaluation requirements.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim a security gap, incident, regulatory exposure, or procurement need.
signals.rationale: Trust milestones can shape buying criteria across industries.

signals.label: Public evidence of platform or architecture modernization
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (migration OR modernization OR platform OR architecture OR cloud OR API-first OR event-driven)
signals.applicability: Companies with first-party engineering, product, or partner evidence of a material platform change.
disqualifiers: Job description keyword without program evidence
signals.safe_interpretation: The company has publicly described a material technology change relevant to integration or operating questions.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim legacy pain, migration failure, available budget, or a need to replace tools.
signals.rationale: Modernization is portable when evidenced by first-party implementation detail.

signals.label: New first-party customer proof or case study
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (customer story OR case study OR customers) (results OR outcome OR achieved)
signals.applicability: Companies publishing dated customer proof relevant to the target audience or campaign.
disqualifiers: Case is unrelated to the campaign
signals.safe_interpretation: The company is emphasizing a particular customer, use case, or outcome in its market narrative.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not independently verify company-published outcomes or generalize one case to all customers.
signals.rationale: Customer proof reveals positioning and audience priorities across sectors.

signals.label: Observable category or positioning change
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (platform OR category OR rebrand OR positioning OR vision) (introduces OR announces OR becomes OR future)
signals.applicability: Companies whose first-party language shows a material change in category, audience, or value proposition.
signals.safe_interpretation: The company is changing how it describes the market, product, audience, or value it owns.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim the prior narrative failed or that the market accepts the new category.
signals.rationale: Narrative shifts are directly relevant to GTM research and portable across industries.

signals.label: Executive presents a specific operating priority
signals.query_template: "{{company_name}}" (speaker OR session OR keynote OR panel) site:{{company_domain}} OR site:youtube.com
signals.applicability: A named company executive speaks substantively about a campaign-relevant priority.
signals.safe_interpretation: The executive has publicly discussed the named priority and language can inform research.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not treat attendance or speaking as purchase intent, budget, or permission to contact.
signals.rationale: Substantive public statements can reveal language; event presence alone is weak.

signals.label: Leadership states an efficiency or productivity priority
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (efficiency OR productivity OR cost-savings OR operating leverage OR margin) (strategy OR priorities OR earnings OR annual)
signals.applicability: Companies with an attributable, dated first-party statement about efficiency, productivity, cost, or operating leverage.
signals.safe_interpretation: Efficiency is an explicit priority; a campaign may test a specific workflow against it.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim distress, layoffs, budget cuts, or quantified savings unless stated.
signals.rationale: Efficiency language is portable but must stay tied to a specific workflow.

signals.label: Documented service, reliability, or operational incident
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (status OR incident OR outage OR disruption OR postmortem)
signals.applicability: Companies with a dated first-party status update or postmortem relevant to the campaign workflow.
disqualifiers: Resolved incident with no campaign relevance
signals.safe_interpretation: A documented incident identifies a real operating condition and the company's stated response.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not exploit an incident, claim continuing failure, or imply the company lacks a solution.
signals.rationale: First-party operational evidence is stronger than anecdotal complaints and still requires tact.

signals.label: Partner or channel program expansion
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (partner program OR channel OR ecosystem OR marketplace) (expands OR launches OR new OR growth)
signals.applicability: Companies announcing a material change in their partner, channel, or marketplace motion.
disqualifiers: Award announcement without a program change
signals.safe_interpretation: The company is investing publicly in a partner or channel motion that may create enablement or coordination questions.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim channel conflict, partner underperformance, or a need for outside help.
signals.rationale: Partner-motion changes are portable and especially useful for ecosystem GTM research.

signals.label: Sustained first-party content focus on a specific problem
signals.query_template: site:{{company_domain}} (blog OR resources OR guides) "{{company_name}}"
signals.applicability: Companies publishing multiple recent first-party assets around the same campaign-relevant problem.
disqualifiers: SEO content with no company point of view
signals.safe_interpretation: Repeated content shows the topic is part of the company's current market narrative.
signals.prohibited_inference: Do not claim internal priority, budget, or product adoption from content volume alone.
signals.rationale: Content concentration is a weak-to-medium signal that becomes useful when paired with stronger evidence.
